payload.feature:
FIX #403 ON macOS AGAIN (PR #483) on branch story-403-process-tree, already checked out in this worktree. HEAD is 72c7937d (on main 78938e53), or a landing commit above it: keep any commit the landing added.

PR #483's test (macos-latest) job, run on a23f8dd3, fails 4 brokkr-protocol unit tests (cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib). Everything else passes on macOS, including the 5 CLI tests the last macOS fix answered. The failures, as CI printed them:

1. process::tests::a_running_driver_adopts_its_trees_orphans (tests.rs, around line 1449): "the orphan's parent", left Some(1), right Some(<leader>). macOS has no subreaper, so the orphan goes to launchd. The test states Linux behaviour.
2. process::tests::a_job_orphaned_before_the_tracker_saw_it_is_ended_before_the_report (the orphaned("job") helper, around line 1516): the report lists a surviving pid where [] is expected. This is the macOS residual the operator ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28: a descendant that leaves the group and whose parent exits between two table reads is reparented to launchd unseen. On CI the orphan was left running.
3. process::tests::an_attempt_whose_end_cannot_be_proven_parks (around line 877), the `unreadable` case (driver `exit 0`, injected table without the engine's row): left Kill { group, errno: 1 }, right Table { error: "the table has no row for the engine itself (pid …)" }.
4. process::tests::a_recorded_descendant_whose_row_loses_its_stamp_parks_the_attempt (around line 1505): left Unresolved { reason: Kill { group, errno: 1 } }, right Unresolved { reason: Signal { pid: <grandchild>, error: "the ps row \"<pid> 1 <pid> S\" could not be read" } }.

The cause of 3 and 4: on Darwin, killpg on a group whose leader is an unreaped zombie returns EPERM. tree::group_refused (tree.rs, around lines 300-314) reads the table, the read fails, and the EPERM refusal stands. Live::kill (attempts.rs, around lines 287-299) then reports the group refusal ahead of the identities' refusal. Both outcomes are fail-closed and unresolved; only the reason reported is wrong. Linux never returns EPERM for a zombie-only group, which is why Linux reports the table's own failure.

Fix, fail-closed, with Linux behaviour unchanged:
- A. When a group EPERM cannot be read against the table because the read fails, the group refusal yields to what the read shows. Report the first identity refusal if an identity kill was refused; otherwise report Unsettled::Table with the read's own error text, exactly as the other table-read failures render it. Every other group refusal (EPERM with a member running, or any other errno) keeps its current reason and its current precedence. Keep the change within CC 15 and a typed return; no Option<Option<…>> tangle.
- B. Gate tests 1 and 2 with #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]. Test 1: macOS has no subreaper. Test 2: the ruled macOS residual. Give each doc comment one line saying why, and name the 2026-09-28 ruling on test 2. Keep a_grandchild_cannot_join_the_engines_group_to_outlive_the_report (orphaned("joiner")) running on both hosts: it passes on macOS. Leave unused-import or dead-code fallout from the gating to clippy on both targets, and check with `cargo clippy -p brokkr-protocol --all-targets --target aarch64-apple-darwin` if that target is installed. Otherwise say in notes that macOS CI decides.
- C. Pin A on this Linux host through the injected seams: an EPERM group refusal (host.kill_group returning Errno::PERM) with an unreadable injected table reports Table, with its exact error; and with a refused identity it reports that Signal. Keep the existing a_group_refused_with_eperm_is_gone_only_when_the_table_shows_it_gone assertions. Add a compiling removal control (the EPERM refusal standing when the read fails again) and record it.

State in your notes, for each of the four CI failures, why the change answers it on macOS: 3 and 4 through A, 1 and 2 through B. Do not change the tests' expected values for 3 and 4. They are what Linux reports, and A makes macOS report the same.

Test stubs must not leak: after the suites, run `pgrep -f` for your stub markers and quote the empty result. Tests need GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 unset if they touch git. Planted pids in unit tests stay above 1,000,000,000.

Gates, all clean, from the worktree root:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-protocol -p brokkr-runtime, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --test suppressions --test agent_fallback --test agent_readouts
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files and clones
- git diff --check origin/main..HEAD

Keep tree.rs's header and the proposed 0006 addendum true to A (the EPERM group read, as 72c7937d states it), and keep the addendum PROPOSED. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run everything in the foreground and never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending.

Commit: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "protocol: <what changed> (#403)", ending with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Every claim in your notes points to a command you ran and what it printed.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. The ruled #403 residuals are not findings.

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.


result.notes:
One signed-off commit, 4e5853a6, above 72c7937d. Not pushed.

A. tree::group_refused now returns Option<GroupRefusal>, a typed enum with two variants. Stands(Errno) covers an EPERM with a member running and every other errno; each keeps its Unsettled::Kill reason and still comes ahead of the identities. Unread(Unsettled) covers an EPERM whose read_table failed; it holds the read's own Unsettled::Table. Live::kill now matches on it: None gives the identities' result, Stands gives Err(Kill), and Unread gives identities.and(Err(unread)), so the first refused identity wins and otherwise the read's error does. Both functions are small, well under CC 15. On Linux the only path that changes is EPERM with a failed read. Linux never returns that for a zombie group, as the framing states. tree.rs's header and the 0006 addendum now state this reading, and the addendum still reads 'proposed' (docs/decisions/0006 line 63).

B. Two tests are now #[cfg(target_os = "linux")], each with a one-line doc reason: a_running_driver_adopts_its_trees_orphans (macOS has no subreaper) and a_job_orphaned_before_the_tracker_saw_it_is_ended_before_the_report (the macOS residual the 2026-09-28 ruling accepted). a_grandchild_cannot_join_the_engines_group_to_outlive_the_report is not gated. On dead-code fallout: grep shows every helper these two tests use (accepting, spawned, deadline_failure, gone, table::snapshot) has other callers. The 'job'/'job-engine' roles are reached through the string dispatch at tests.rs:1055/1060, which is still compiled. `cargo clippy -p brokkr-protocol --all-targets --target aarch64-apple-darwin` printed "can't find crate for `core` ... the `aarch64-apple-darwin` target may not be installed", so macOS CI decides clippy on Darwin.

C. In attempts/tests.rs, a_group_refused_with_eperm_is_gone_only_when_the_table_shows_it_gone keeps its zombies, exiting, populated and EINVAL assertions. One assertion had to change: the unreadable-table case used to expect Kill, and A requires it to report the read's failure. It now expects Unsettled::Table { error: TableError::NoSelf{pid:0}.to_string() } and pins the exact text "the process table could not be read: the table has no row for the engine itself (pid 0)". Two new cases: a recorded identity whose kill is refused (kill: forbidden) under the same unreadable EPERM gives Signal { pid: RECORDED, error: EPERM }, and with the recorded set cleared the same host gives the Table error again. Planted pids are GROUP/RECORDED, both 1,000,000,00x.

Removal controls, both compiling, both run and then restored:
(1) The EPERM stands again when the read fails: tree.rs `Err(_unread) => Some(GroupRefusal::Stands(errno))`. The test failed at attempts/tests.rs:518 with left Err(Kill { group: 1000000001, errno: 1 }), right Err(Table { error: "the table has no row for the engine itself (pid 0)" }).
(2) The unread refusal is reported ahead of the identities: attempts.rs `Err::<(), _>(unread).and(identities)`. The test failed at attempts/tests.rs:535 with left Err(Table {...}), right Err(Signal { pid: 1000000002, error: "Operation not permitted (os error 1)" }).
After restoring, the attempts:: tests passed 10/10.

Why each macOS CI failure is answered (not observed on macOS; this host is Linux, and macOS CI must confirm):
1 (a_running_driver_adopts_its_trees_orphans, Some(1) vs Some(leader)): B. The test is Linux only because macOS has no subreaper.
2 (orphaned("job") surviving pid): B. It is the macOS residual ruled on 2026-09-28, now Linux only.
3 (an_attempt_whose_end_cannot_be_proven_parks, the `unreadable` case): through A. Darwin's EPERM on the zombie-led group now meets the failed read (no engine row) as Unread. No identity is refused, so Live::kill returns that read's Unsettled::Table, which is what Linux reports. The expected value is unchanged.
4 (a_recorded_descendant_whose_row_loses_its_stamp_parks_the_attempt): through A. The EPERM's read fails on the stampless row, giving Unread, and it yields to the refused identity kill, Signal { pid: grandchild, error: the ps row ... could not be read }, which is what Linux reports. The expected value is unchanged.

members.adversarial: Adversarial review of the landing commit 4e5853a6 above 72c7937d (git rev-list --count 72c7937d..HEAD = 1; git status --porcelain empty). A: tree::group_refused now returns Option<GroupRefusal>, Stands(Errno) or Unread(Unsettled::Table); Live::kill returns identities.and(Err(unread)) for Unread, else Err(Kill) for Stands. I traced every arm: Ok/ESRCH -> None -> identities; non-EPERM -> Stands -> Kill; EPERM + read Ok with no running member -> None; EPERM + read Ok with a running member -> Stands -> Kill; EPERM + read Err -> Unread, always Err (first identity Signal, else the read's Table). Every outcome parks; no fail-open path. B: the two tests carry #[cfg(target_os = "linux")] with the required one-line reasons and the 2026-09-28 ruling named on the orphaned job test; a_grandchild_cannot_join_the_engines_group_to_outlive_the_report stays ungated. I independently reproduced both recorded removal controls by sed edit then cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib -- a_group_refused_with_eperm_is_gone_only_when_the_table_shows_it_gone: mutation 1 (Err(_unread) => Stands(errno)) FAILED at attempts/tests.rs:518 left Err(Kill { group: 1000000001, errno: 1 }) right Err(Table { error: "the table has no row for the engine itself (pid 0)" }); mutation 2 (Err::<(), _>(unread).and(identities)) FAILED at :535 left Err(Table {...}) right Err(Signal { pid: 1000000002, ... }); each restored and git status --short empty. To test the macOS gating's dead-code/unused fallout on this host I forced #[cfg(any())] on the two gated tests and ran cargo clippy -p brokkr-protocol --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings: exit 0, no warning; restored. Gates I ran from the worktree root with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 unset: cargo fmt --all -- --check OK; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings exit 0; cargo test -p brokkr-protocol -p brokkr-runtime exit 0 (my rerun; the implementer's log .forge/test-proto-runtime.log shows protocol lib 502 passed/1 ignored, runtime lib 517 passed, 0 FAILED); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --test suppressions --test agent_fallback --test agent_readouts exit 0 (496 lib, 7 fallback, 5 readouts, 6+1 ignored suppressions); typos --hidden OK; quality/ratchet.sh files 'ratchet: file size holds' and clones 'ratchet: duplication holds'; git diff --check origin/main..HEAD exit 0.
